Thank you Mr. Williams. Good afternoon committee members. My name is Veronica Blair and I'm the policy manager with the community standards department.
This report provides context for a request from the Broadway business improvement district to wave parking fees associated with our community patio project.

The bid is proposing to construct a patio within four paid parking spaces at the end of 12th street east adjacent to Broadway Avenue. The patio would be in place starting this year from June to mid September over the course of five years.
The city is a funding partner in this project through urban design and under our agreement with the bid our contributions cannot be used to cover any rental fees associated with the parking spaces.
Across the city the rental of paid parking spaces falls under the temporary reserve parking program which charges rental fees based on an hourly parking rate.
Reductions to the parking rental fee have been approved by council for three instances. The first being the mobile food truck program.
Secondly, parking patio is directly associated with a restaurant lounge or tavern and special event related reservations.

The bid's project does not meet the criteria of any of the three reduced rental parking rates including the discounted parking patio rate due to not being associated with a restaurant lounge or tavern.
Under the temporary reserve parking program, the bid's patio would pay just under $12,000 per year.
The bid's request for a full waiver of these parking fees is outside of current city policy, which is why they've approached the committee in council with this request.
If the committee in council will see fit to apply the reduced parking patio rate for the bid's project, the bid would pay approximately $4,600 per year rather than $12,000.
It's noted that the report was provided as information since administration does not have a policy mechanism to support the full waiver of fees.
The intent was to provide the committee with relevant information on similar programs.
That being said, while not associated with a restaurant, the bid's patio meets many of the same objectives that the city is looking for with its parking patio program.
And applying a similar rate as the parking patio would be a reasonable compromise.
